name: East Face

text.approach: Drive the Harts Pass road over the pass and down the Slate Creek road to the locked gate (about 3,800 ft). Walk the old South Fork Slate Creek road roughly a mile to the large bridge near 4,000 ft, then leave the road and travel south through open forest.
text.overview: The approach most climbers use: a bushwhack from the Slate Creek road to the east ridge, a steep vegetated slot, scrambling into the east cirque, then a ledge traverse to the summit gully on the west side of the top block.
text.descent: Retrace the route; descend the green slot carefully and keep to the forest on the left on the way down to avoid the alder.

A lengthy snow ramp climbs nearly straight up. Rock bands may show near 12,600 feet and 13,300 depending on snow. name: Cloudy Peak Traverse (South Ridge)

text.approach: Approach as for the East Route to Lyman Lake: either from Lake Chelan via Lucerne, Holden Village and the Railroad Creek trail, or from the Chiwawa River side via Phelps Creek, over Spider Gap and down past the Upper Lyman Lakes. Both ways have been closed in recent seasons, the Lucerne side by storm-damaged roads and the Chiwawa side by wildfire and road closures, so check current Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest closures before planning. From Lower Lyman Lake follow Trail #1256 west through forest and meadows to Cloudy Pass (6,440 ft), and gain the ridge crest there to start the traverse.
text.overview: A harder alternative approached from the west: gain the crest at Cloudy Pass, follow the ridge over Cloudy Peak (7,915 ft), then descend and cross talus to North Star's summit block via the same short, exposed Class 3-4 step used by the East Route.
text.descent: From the North Star summit, downclimb the summit step, then make a direct beeline across talus toward the Cloudy Pass Trail, intersecting it at about 6,300 ft; follow meadows and interconnected granite slabs roughly 1.5 miles back to Cloudy Pass/Lyman Lake basin.

waypoints.name: Cloudy Pass
waypoints.directions: Cloudy Pass is on Trail #1256, which climbs west from Lower Lyman Lake through open forest and meadows. Lyman Lake is reached up Railroad Creek from Holden Village, or from Phelps Creek over Spider Gap and down past the Upper Lyman Lakes.

waypoints.name: North Star Mountain summit
waypoints.directions: From the pass, turn right and follow the ridge northeast up to Cloudy Peak (7,915 ft). Beyond it, lose elevation off its east side, either down the east ridge with some Class 3-4 or by dropping south of the summit around a cliff band, to reach the talus slopes that connect to North Star. Follow them northeast to the final 100 ft of rock to the summit, which is slick with lichen when wet.

name: Jaw's Tooth and Northwest Ridge

text.overview: Off Skookum's north ridge stands Jaw's Tooth, a shark-tooth pinnacle of 65 feet; the two combine into a fine route. Start in the basin northwest of Skookum and zigzag upward through fourth class and low fifth class ground to the striking layback corner, a sustained, very high quality 5.6 pitch. Easy ground leads to the tooth's summit. Getting down into the southern notch means either a rappel off tat or a low 5th downclimb. name: East Face

text.approach: Ferry/floatplane to Stehekin (no road access), then the Company Creek Trail roughly 3 miles to a point below Tupshin's west side. Leave the trail and scramble up White Goat Mountain's west slopes through dense brush, traversing rightward through the 4,200-4,600 ft band, then cross a roughly 7,200 ft pass above Bird Lakes and descend into the Bird Lakes basin below Tupshin's east face (face starts ~7,600 ft). Most parties in July to September go in by the Devore Creek trail to the Bird Creek camp near 5,400-5,500 ft, then fight slide alder up to a basin camp around 5,800 ft; easy slopes lead to a ridge near 7,000 ft, then a descending traverse to the snow basin east of the summit block.

text.overview: A longer, harder technical line up Tupshin's east face, reached via a demanding cross-country approach from Company Creek over a pass above Bird Lakes; class 2-4 ledge scrambling leads to a short, poorly-protected 5.4-5.6 crux below the summit.
text.descent: Downclimb the summit pitch and upper class 4 terrain back through the ledge system, taking care around the crux flake/crack; parties have used a 30 m rope for the technical sections. Continue down the zigzagging ledges and the lower class 2-3 ramp back to the basin below the face, then reverse the cross-country traverse over the pass above Bird Lakes to Company Creek Trail.

name: North Ridge

text.approach: Park on the wide paved shoulder of SR-20 about three quarters of a mile west of the signed Blue Lake trailhead lot, on the north side, where there is no guard rail. A good climbers' trail leads from the road through forest into the basin. No pass is needed at the pullout; the Blue Lake lot needs a forest pass.
text.road: {"name":"SR-20 (North Cascades Highway)","status":"seasonal","driveNote":"SR-20 closes for winter, normally from about mid-November to mid-April."}
text.overview: The north ridge is the rock route on Whistler, climbed from the highway shoulder shared with Cutthroat Peak. A climbers' trail drops into the open basin between the two peaks, then the route follows the ridge to the summit pyramid, mostly class 3 with some class 4 steps, over about 2,700 ft of gain. The ridge is exposed in places, and a fall would have serious consequences.
text.descent: Retrace the ridge. A short loose step is usually rappelled instead of downclimbed.
